thm-nonlinear-least-squares-gradient-and:
## Statement

Let $n,m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let
$r=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)^T:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be of class $C^2$ (each component
has continuous partial derivatives through order two, as in
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]). Define
$$\phi(x):=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)^2=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2,$$
and let $J(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be the Jacobian with $i$th row
$\nabla r_i(x)^T$. Then $\phi$ is of class $C^2$ and
$$\nabla\phi(x)=J(x)^T r(x),\qquad \nabla^2\phi(x)=J(x)^TJ(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)\nabla^2r_i(x).$$

The second term in the Hessian is the residual-curvature term. It vanishes
when $r(x)=0$, but need not vanish at a nonzero-residual stationary point.
lem-nonlinear-residual-linearization-err:
## Statement

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ with
$m,n\ge1$, and let $J(x)=Dr(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$. Let $K\subseteq U$
be convex and let $x_*,x\in K$. Suppose $L\ge0$ and
$\|J(y)-J(z)\|_2\le L\|y-z\|_2$ for all $y,z\in K$, where the matrix norm is
the Euclidean induced operator norm of [[def-induced-matrix-p-norm]]. Then
$$\|r(x)-r(x_*)-J(x)(x-x_*)\|_2\le\tfrac L2\|x-x_*\|_2^2.$$
The dimensions $m$ and $n$ need not be equal.
lem-levenberg-marquardt-step-is-scaled-t:
## Statement

Let $J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $r\in\mathbb R^m$, $m,n\ge1$, let
$D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be nonsingular, let $\lambda>0$, and put
$g:=J^Tr$. Assume $g\ne0$. There is a unique $p_\lambda$ satisfying
$$\bigl(J^TJ+\lambda D^TD\bigr)p_\lambda=-g.$$
Set $z_\lambda:=Dp_\lambda$, $\widetilde J:=JD^{-1}$, and
$\Delta_\lambda:=\|z_\lambda\|_2>0$. Then $z_\lambda$ uniquely minimizes
$$q_\lambda(z):=\tfrac12\|r+\widetilde Jz\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|z\|_2^2$$
over $\mathbb R^n$, and globally minimizes the unregularized model
$$m(z):=\tfrac12\|r+\widetilde Jz\|_2^2$$
over the trust-region ball $\|z\|_2\le\Delta_\lambda$ of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]]. Its predicted reduction is
positive and, in the original step coordinates,
$$m(0)-m(Dp_\lambda)=\tfrac12\|Jp_\lambda\|_2^2+\lambda\|Dp_\lambda\|_2^2>0.$$
alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-s:
## Definition

Input a stored residual $r\in\mathbb R^m$, a stored Jacobian $J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$ (using the convention of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), a factorization mode QR or SVD, and a declared singular-value threshold $\tau\ge0$. A computed QR report may also carry a verified full-rank certificate $s>0$ asserting $\|Jv\|_2\ge s\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. The target exact step, when it is returned, is the unique minimizer of $\frac12\|r+Jp\|_2^2$ and hence solves $J^TJp=-J^Tr$; this target is asserted only on a full-column-rank branch. Do not form $J^TJ$ in either solve path.

For QR mode, either supply an exact reduced factorization $J=QR$ with $Q^TQ=I_n$, or compute one by setting $C=[J\mid-r]$ and, for $k=1,\ldots,n$, applying [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] to the active part of column $k$ and all trailing columns of $C$, including its last right-hand-side column. Propagate the first factorization failure. In exact mode, a zero diagonal in $R$ returns rank-deficient; otherwise solve $Rp=Q^T(-r)$ by backward substitution and return exact-step($p$). In computed mode, a zero diagonal returns rank-deficient-candidate; a failed triangular solve returns linear-solve-failure; and a nonzero computed diagonal without an independently supplied full-rank certificate returns rank-unverified with the computed candidate but no full-rank claim. With a full-rank certificate, return computed-candidate($p$). The computed-QR backward-stability conclusion of [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] is attached only when all of that theorem's successful-execution, arithmetic, and nonsingularity hypotheses are supplied; otherwise no backward-stability conclusion is returned.

For SVD mode, the input includes an exact factorization $J=U\Sigma V^T$, or a computed report containing finite stored factors $\widehat U_1$, $\widehat\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_i)$ with nonnegative entries, and $\widehat V$, together with certified intervals $[\ell_i,u_i]$ satisfying $\ell_i\le\sigma_i(J)\le u_i$ for each of the $n$ singular values relevant to full column rank. In the exact case, if any $\sigma_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold and no Gauss-Newton step. If every $\sigma_i>\tau$, return
$$p=-V\,\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\sigma_n^{-1})\,U_1^Tr,$$
where $U_1$ consists of the corresponding $n$ left singular vectors. For a computed report, if any $u_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold; if any interval satisfies $\ell_i\le\tau<u_i$, return rank-unverified; if every lower endpoint exceeds $\tau$ but some stored $\widehat\sigma_i=0$, return factorization-failure; otherwise return the finite candidate
$$\widehat p=-\widehat V\,\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\widehat\sigma_n^{-1})\,\widehat U_1^Tr$$
with status computed-candidate and make no accuracy claim beyond the supplied report. The certified intervals determine only the threshold branch; no computed-SVD accuracy bound is asserted. A computed SVD routine is not defined here; the SVD branch consumes its report.

If $m<n$, return unsupported-shape; if the selected factorization reports failure, return factorization-failure; every status other than exact-step is explicitly not a certified exact full-rank Gauss-Newton step.
alg-safeguarded-levenberg-marquardt:
## Definition

This algorithm performs one finite-budget LM trial update. Inputs are $x\in U$, a residual function $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$, its Jacobian $J(x)$, a fixed nonsingular $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, a floor $\lambda_{\min}>0$, current damping $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$, factors $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, a trust radius $\Delta>0$, and an attempt cap $N\ge1$. A computed run may include a certificate that the exact scalar product $J(x)^Tr(x)$ is zero. Put $\phi(x)=\|r(x)\|_2^2/2$ and $m_0(p)=\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2/2$. The returned step is obtained by minimizing
$$\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Dp\|_2^2,$$
which is equivalent to solving
$$(J(x)^TJ(x)+\lambda D^TD)p=-J(x)^Tr(x).$$
For stable linear algebra, form $A_\lambda=[J(x);\sqrt\lambda D]$ and $s_\lambda=[r(x);0]$, then call [[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]] in QR mode on $(A_\lambda,s_\lambda)$. The exact augmented matrix has full column rank because $D$ is nonsingular and $\lambda>0$. A computed-candidate status remains a candidate and carries no convergence guarantee.

For attempts $j=1,\ldots,N$, do the following.

1. If the linear solver reports a factorization, rank, or solve failure, return linear-solve-failure with its report. In exact arithmetic, if $J(x)^Tr(x)=0$, return stationary without forming a ratio. In a computed run, return stationary only with the supplied certificate that this exact gradient is zero; a rounded zero without such a certificate returns gradient-unverified and no ratio.
2. For a nonzero trial $p$, compute $\operatorname{pred}=m_0(0)-m_0(p)$. If $\operatorname{pred}\le0$, return nonpositive-predicted-decrease; do not compute a ratio.
3. If $x+p\notin U$ or $\|Dp\|_2>\Delta$, reject the trial, set $\lambda\leftarrow\gamma\lambda$, and continue. If the damping update is not representable in the selected arithmetic, return damping-range-failure.
4. Otherwise compute $\operatorname{ared}=\phi(x)-\phi(x+p)$ and $\rho=\operatorname{ared}/\operatorname{pred}$. If $\rho<\eta_1$, reject and set $\lambda\leftarrow\gamma\lambda$. If this was attempt $N$, return rejection-budget-exhausted; otherwise continue.
5. If $\rho\ge\eta_1$, accept and return $x+p$, $p$, $\rho$, and the next damping. If also $\rho\ge\eta_2$ and $\|Dp\|_2=\Delta$, set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\max\{\lambda_{\min},\lambda/\gamma\}$; in every other accepted case set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\lambda$. A failed function evaluation returns trial-evaluation-failure.

If all $N$ attempts are rejected, return rejection-budget-exhausted. The equality in the boundary test is exact for exact arithmetic and is the equality test on stored values in a computed run. No claim is made that every finite budget succeeds.
thm-gauss-newton-local-linear-contractio:
## Statement

Let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^2$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let
$\phi=\|r\|_2^2/2$, $J=Dr$, $A=J^TJ$, and
$S(x)=\sum_i r_i(x)\nabla^2r_i(x)$. Let $x_*\in U$ satisfy
$J(x_*)^Tr(x_*)=0$, and let the closed ball
$B=\{x:\|x-x_*\|_2\le R\}$ lie in $U$, with $R>0$. Suppose on $B$:

- $J(x)$ has full column rank and smallest singular value at least $\sigma>0$;
- $\|J(x)\|_2\le M$;
- $J$ is $L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean induced matrix norm;
- $\|S(x)\|_2\le\kappa$.

Define $q=(\kappa+MLR)/\sigma^2$ and assume $q<1$. For the exact full-rank
Gauss-Newton step $p(x)=-A(x)^{-1}J(x)^Tr(x)$, every $x\in B$ satisfies
$$\|x+p(x)-x_*\|_2\le q\|x-x_*\|_2.$$
Consequently the exact iterates from any $x_0\in B$ stay in $B$ and converge
to $x_*$ at a linear rate no larger than $q$. The curvature hypothesis
controls the residual term $S$; no quadratic rate is claimed when it is
nonzero.
thm-gauss-newton-zero-residual-quadratic:
## Statement

Let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and let
$x_*\in U$ satisfy $r(x_*)=0$. Let $B=\{x:\|x-x_*\|_2\le R\}\subseteq U$ be
convex. Suppose $J=Dr$ is $L$-Lipschitz on $B$ and, for some $\sigma>0$,
$$\|J(x)v\|_2\ge\sigma\|v\|_2\qquad(x\in B,\ v\in\mathbb R^n).$$
Thus every $J(x)$ has full column rank. For the exact Gauss-Newton iteration
$x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$, where $p_k$ is the unique minimizer of
$\|r(x_k)+J(x_k)p\|_2^2$, set $C=L/(2\sigma)$. Then every $x_k\in B$ satisfies
$$\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|_2\le C\|x_k-x_*\|_2^2.$$
If $C>0$ and $\|x_0-x_*\|_2\le\min\{R,1/(2C)\}$, all iterates stay in the ball,
converge to $x_*$, and contract at least by $1/2$ per iteration after the
quadratic estimate. If $C=0$, one exact step reaches $x_*$. This result concerns
exact solves; it asserts no finite-precision convergence rate.
lem-levenberg-marquardt-large-damping-fo:
## Statement

Let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let
$J=Dr$, and let $\phi=\|r\|_2^2/2$. Fix $x_0\in U$ and suppose its sublevel set
$S=\{x\in U:\phi(x)\le\phi(x_0)\}$ is compact. Put
$S_1=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{dist}(y,S)\le1\}$ and assume $S_1\subseteq U$.
On $S_1$, suppose $\|r(x)\|_2\le R_0$, $\|J(x)\|_2\le M$, and $J$ is
$L$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean induced matrix norm.
Fix nonsingular $D$, numbers $d,d_+>0$ with
$\|Dv\|_2\ge d\|v\|_2$ and
$\max\{\|D\|_2,\|D^T\|_2\}\le d_+$, and parameters
$\lambda_{\min}>0$, $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, and $\Delta>0$.
Define
$$C_D:=d_+^2+M^2/\lambda_{\min},\quad C_E:=\tfrac L2(R_0+M)+\tfrac{L^2}{8},\quad P:=\min\{1,\Delta/(2d_+)\},$$
$$\Lambda:=\max\left\{\lambda_{\min},\frac{MR_0}{d^2P},\frac{C_EC_D^2}{(1-\eta_2)d^6}\right\},\quad N:=1+\left\lceil\frac{\log(\Lambda/\lambda_{\min})}{\log\gamma}\right\rceil.$$
At any $x\in S$ with $g:=\nabla\phi(x)=J(x)^Tr(x)\ne0$, an exact LM trial with damping
$\lambda\ge\Lambda$ has $0<\operatorname{pred}$, $\|Dp_\lambda\|_2\le\Delta/2$,
and $\rho\ge\eta_2$. Therefore, if the algorithm starts an iteration with
$\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$ and has at least $N$ trials, it either accepts an
earlier trial with $\rho\ge\eta_1$ or accepts by the $N$th trial. This conclusion
assumes exact subproblem solves and exact objective evaluations.
thm-safeguarded-levenberg-marquardt-glob:
## Statement

Let $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let
$\phi=\|r\|_2^2/2$, and fix $x_0\in U$. Suppose the initial sublevel
$S=\{x\in U:\phi(x)\le\phi(x_0)\}$ is compact, its closed unit neighborhood
$S_1=\{y:\operatorname{dist}(y,S)\le1\}$ lies in $U$, and on $S_1$ the
Jacobian $J=Dr$ is $L$-Lipschitz with
$\|J(x)\|_2\le M$ and $\|r(x)\|_2\le R_0$.
Fix nonsingular $D$ and constants $d,d_+>0$ such that
$\|Dv\|_2\ge d\|v\|_2$ and
$\max\{\|D\|_2,\|D^T\|_2\}\le d_+$.
Choose $\lambda_{\min}>0$, $\lambda_0\ge\lambda_{\min}$, $\gamma>1$,
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, and $\Delta>0$, and define $C_D,C_E,P,\Lambda,N$ as
in [[lem-levenberg-marquardt-large-damping-forces-sufficient-decrease]].
Run [[alg-safeguarded-levenberg-marquardt]] in exact arithmetic with at least
$N$ trials per iteration, exact subproblem solves, and no evaluation failures.

The run either terminates at an iterate with $J(x_k)^Tr(x_k)=0$, or every
nonstationary iteration is accepted and
$$\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_{k+1})\ge\eta_1 c\,\|J(x_k)^Tr(x_k)\|_2^2,\qquad c:=\frac{\lambda_{\min}d^2}{\bigl(M^2+\lambda_{\max}d_+^2\bigr)^2},$$
where $\lambda_{\max}:=\max\{\lambda_0,\gamma\Lambda\}$.
Consequently $\|J(x_k)^Tr(x_k)\|_2\to0$, and every accumulation point is
stationary. This does not imply $r(x_k)\to0$; the method certifies first-order
stationarity of the least-squares objective, not exact data fit.
